summary: The bill directs the Election Assistance Commission to award grants to states and localities to buy or maintain electronic pollbooks that track and share real-time voter wait times at polling places, and requires public online posting of that wait-time data after each election.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $120,000,000 in new appropriations to the Election Assistance Commission for grants to states and jurisdictions to procure and maintain e-pollbooks and related wait-time technology. This directly expands federal spending on election infrastructure.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or systems.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, borders, or citizenship.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net benefits.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
While the bill authorizes new spending, it does not address deficit reduction, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy priorities around the national debt.

The bill includes a nondiscrimination clause in training requirements that references sexual orientation, but this is incidental language and does not expand or limit legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.

The bill funds electronic pollbooks and wait-time reporting systems specifically to reduce polling-place wait times and improve voter information for federal elections. This directly facilitates and expands access to voting.
The bill funds voting technology and requires compliance with a federal certification program, but it does not address data privacy, surveillance, or broader tech regulation.
The bill contains no provisions related to unions, collective bargaining, or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions addressing religious exemptions or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
